title: Minimal Reversal Budgets for Equilibrium Responses in Signed Feedback Networks
banked_reason: Stage -1.2 (single-artifact) mode=revise returned needs-pivot — angle 0 not authorable as posed
gap_reasons: Give the tie question a worked rational primitive instance with its two active branches, covariance correlation, tangent cones, and the induced Gaussian experiment; this makes the claimed residual and consumer testable.
The v3 directive is mathematically impossible within the preserved reciprocal-contact kernel.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery revised an incremental three-node reversal-budget classification toward a field-tier inference theorem at an axis/cap versus interior contact tie. Strict convexity forces smooth pasting at those ties, making the proposed distinct-gradient Gaussian experiment impossible; an independent validity check confirmed this. The deterministic placement, allocation, and rational-certificate claims remain unproved presolve material for a separately vetted lower-tier run.
tldr: For one fixed reciprocal candidate-link pair, the compact target is the least capped weighted budget needed to reverse a three-node equilibrium response, mapped to \([0,1]\). The fifteen-placement theorem is a deterministic screening result; inference uses only the reciprocal contact map. Generic projection is retained as an honest but conservative baseline. On separated unique-contact strata, an explicit scalar score interval attains the regular local minimax bound and is strictly shorter than ten-dimensional Wald projection. At a genuine axis--interior or cap--interior tie, the Gaussian minimum experiment is explicit, but its minimax expected-length bound and adaptive attaining procedure remain an open-ended question, so no field-tier adaptation claim is made.
gap: Inverse-sign papers do not solve capped weighted contact, while generic set-projection and directional-inference papers do not supply the target-specific two-branch minimax adaptation theorem.
fill: The settled package gives deterministic screening, the reciprocal allocation rule, generic honest projection, explicit branch geometry including \(S=0\), and efficient inference on separated unique-contact strata. The tie-regime adaptation theorem is isolated as the first-class open problem.
